content: Epiglottitis For pediatric patients with epiglottitis, the preferred treatment regimens include: 1. Cefotaxime at a dose of 50 mg/kg administered intravenously every 8 hours. 2. Alternatively, Ceftriaxone at 50–75 mg/kg/day intravenously every 12–24 hours combined with Vancomycin at 10 mg/kg intravenously every 6 hours. For adults with epiglottitis, the preferred treatment regimens include: 1. Cefotaxime at 2 g intravenously every 4–8 hours. 2. Alternatively, Ceftriaxone at 1–2 g/day intravenously every 12–24 hours combined with Vancomycin at 2 g/day intravenously every 6–12 hours. An alternate regimen for both pediatric and adult patients includes Levofloxacin (500 mg IV every 24 hours or 8 mg/kg IV every 12 hours) combined with Clindamycin (20–40 mg/kg/day IV every 6–8 hours for children or 600–1200 mg IV every 6–12 hours for adults). Jugular Vein Phlebitis (Lemierre's Syndrome) Septic jugular thrombophlebitis, also known as Lemierre's syndrome, is commonly caused by pathogens such as Fusobacterium, Viridans streptococci, Staphylococcus, Peptostreptococcus, Bacteroides, and other oral anaerobes. For immunocompetent hosts, the preferred regimens include: 1. Penicillin G at 2–4 million units intravenously every 4–6 hours. 2. Metronidazole at 0.5 g intravenously every 6 hours. 3. Ampicillin-Sulbactam at 2 g intravenously every 4 hours. 4. Clindamycin at 600 mg intravenously every 6 hours. For immunocompromised hosts, the preferred regimens include: 1. Cefotaxime at 2 g intravenously every 6 hours. 2. Ceftizoxime at 4 g intravenously every 8 hours. 3. Piperacillin at 3 g intravenously every 4 hours. 4. Imipenem at 500 mg intravenously every 6 hours. 5. Gatifloxacin at 400 mg intravenously every 24 hours. Laryngitis Antibiotic therapy is not recommended for the treatment of acute laryngitis, as it does not significantly improve objective symptoms. Ludwig's Angina Ludwig's angina is caused by pathogens such as Viridans streptococci, Peptostreptococcus, Bacteroides, and other oral anaerobes. For immunocompetent hosts, the preferred regimens include: 1. Penicillin G (2–4 million units IV every 4–6 hours) combined with Tobramycin (2 mg/kg IV every 8 hours). 2. Ampicillin-Sulbactam at 2 g intravenously every 4 hours. 3. Clindamycin at 600 mg intravenously every 6 hours. 4. Doxycycline at 200 mg intravenously every 12 hours. 5. Cefoxitin at 2 g intravenously every 6 hours. 6. Cefotetan at 2 g intravenously every 12 hours. For immunocompromised hosts, the preferred regimens include: 1. Cefotaxime at 2 g intravenously every 6 hours. 2. Ceftizoxime at 4 g intravenously every 8 hours. 3. Piperacillin at 3 g intravenously every 4 hours. 4. Imipenem at 500 mg intravenously every 6 hours. 5. Meropenem at 1 g intravenously every 8 hours. 6. Gatifloxacin at 200 mg intravenously every 24 hours. Parapharyngeal Space Infection Parapharyngeal space infections are caused by pathogens such as Viridans streptococci, Staphylococcus, Peptostreptococcus, Bacteroides, and other oral anaerobes. For immunocompetent hosts, the preferred regimens include: 1. Penicillin G (2–4 million units IV every 4–6 hours) combined with Metronidazole (0.5 g IV every 6 hours). 2. Ampicillin-Sulbactam at 2 g intravenously every 4 hours. 3. Clindamycin at 600 mg intravenously every 6 hours. For immunocompromised hosts, the preferred regimens include: 1. Cefotaxime at 2 g intravenously every 6 hours. 2. Ceftizoxime at 4 g intravenously every 8 hours. 3. Piperacillin at 3 g intravenously every 4 hours. 4. Imipenem at 500 mg intravenously every 6 hours. 5. Gatifloxacin at 400 mg intravenously every 24 hours. Pharyngitis, Diphtheria For diphtheria, the CDC recommends: 1. Erythromycin (oral or IV) for 14 days at 40 mg/kg per day (maximum 2 g/day). 2. Procaine penicillin G administered intramuscularly for 14 days (300,000 units/day for patients weighing less than 10 kg). For patients with allergies, alternative regimens include Penicillin G, Erythromycin, Rifampin, or Clindamycin. Pharyngitis, Streptococcal For acute streptococcal pharyngitis: In children, the preferred regimen is Penicillin V orally at 250 mg twice or three times daily. In adolescents and adults, the preferred regimens include: 1. Penicillin V orally at 250 mg four times daily or 500 mg twice daily for 10 days. 2. Amoxicillin at 50 mg/kg once daily (maximum 1000 mg) or 25 mg/kg twice daily for 10 days. 3. Benzathine Penicillin G intramuscularly as a single dose (600,000 units for patients under 27 kg; 1,200,000 units for patients 27 kg or more). Alternate regimens include Cephalexin, Cefadroxil, Clindamycin, Azithromycin, or Clarithromycin. For chronic streptococcal pharyngitis, preferred regimens include Clindamycin, Penicillin combined with Rifampin, or Amoxicillin-clavulanate. Sinusitis For acute sinusitis in pediatric patients: Preferred regimens include Amoxicillin at 90 mg/kg/day divided every 12 hours or Amoxicillin-clavulanate (extra strength) for 10–14 days. For adults: Preferred regimens include Amoxicillin (250–500 mg every 8 hours or 500–875 mg every 12 hours) or Amoxicillin-clavulanate (extended-release tablets) for 5–7 days. For chronic sinusitis: Pediatric patients may receive Amoxicillin-clavulanate at 45 mg/kg/day every 12 hours. If MRSA is suspected, Clindamycin is recommended. If anaerobes are involved, Metronidazole can be combined with other antibiotics. For adults, Amoxicillin-clavulanate is the preferred treatment. If anaerobes are involved, Metronidazole can be combined with other agents such as Cefuroxime, Cefdinir, or Levofloxacin. Stomatitis For aphthous stomatitis, topical steroids may help reduce pain and swelling. For herpetic stomatitis, Acyclovir at 15 mg/kg orally every 5 hours for 7 days is recommended. Submandibular Space Infection Submandibular space infections, including Ludwig's angina, are caused by Viridans streptococci, Peptostreptococcus, Bacteroides, and other oral anaerobes. For immunocompetent hosts, preferred regimens include Penicillin G combined with Tobramycin, Ampicillin-Sulbactam, Clindamycin, Doxycycline, Cefoxitin, or Cefotetan. For immunocompromised hosts, preferred regimens include Cefotaxime, Ceftizoxime, Piperacillin, Imipenem, Meropenem, or Gatifloxacin. Tonsillitis For tonsillitis, the preferred treatment is Penicillin V orally for 10 days or Benzathine Penicillin as a single intramuscular dose. Alternate regimens include second-generation cephalosporins, Clindamycin, Azithromycin, Clarithromycin, or Erythromycin. Ulcerative Gingivitis Patients should be instructed on proper oral hygiene and may use a prescription antibacterial mouthwash such as Chlorhexidine 0.12% twice daily. If systemic involvement is present, Amoxicillin (250 mg three times daily for 7 days) with or without Metronidazole is recommended. Vincent's Angina The preferred treatment for Vincent's angina is Penicillin G at 4 million units intravenously every 4 hours. An alternative treatment is Clindamycin at 600 mg intravenously every 8 hours.
